summary.text: Michael Cloud is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Texas's 27th District. A former Victoria County Republican Party chairman, church media director and small-business owner, he first won the seat in a June 2018 special election and has been re-elected since. He serves on the Appropriations and Oversight committees and is seeking another term.

paragraphs.text: Cloud was born in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and graduated from Miamisburg High School in Ohio.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Oral Roberts University.

He worked as media and communications director at Faith Family Church in Victoria, Texas, and owned Bright Ideas Media, according to Ballotpedia, and his official biography describes him as a small business owner and a longtime District 27 resident.
He also served on the Texas State Executive Republican Committee and as chairman of the Victoria County Republican Party.
Cloud won a special election on June 30, 2018, for the 27th District seat, succeeding Rep. Blake Farenthold, and took office on July 10, 2018.
He won a full term in November 2018 with 60.3% of the vote.

In the House he serves on the Appropriations Committee, where Ballotpedia lists him as vice chair of the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Subcommittee, and on the Oversight and Government Reform Committee.
He defeated Chris Hatley in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary to advance to the November general election.
